RESEARCH STRATEGY·CRO LEADERSHIP·TRANSLATIONAL INTERPRETATION

How I can help

Focused scientific support at critical development decisions.

Practical, scoped engagements for emerging biotech teams that need experienced translational leadership without expanding their permanent headcount.

01 / STRATEGY

Translational strategy & evidence-gap assessment

Review efficacy, PK/PD, safety and biomarker data; identify decision-critical gaps; and develop a prioritized study plan with endpoints, sequencing, go/no-go criteria and budget considerations.

Typical output: evidence-gap memo and prioritized research blueprint.

02 / EXECUTION

CRO selection & research oversight

Translate research questions into scopes of work, assess CRO capabilities and proposals, support vendor discussions, and oversee outsourced studies, milestones, data quality and reporting.

Typical output: CRO comparison, study scope and milestone-based oversight plan.

03 / TRANSLATION

Early clinical data & biomarker strategy

Integrate emerging Phase 1 safety, exposure, PK/PD and exploratory biomarker signals to identify unanswered questions and inform dose, population, assay and Phase 2 planning discussions.

Typical output: integrated evidence summary and decision-focused recommendations.

How we can work together

What stage is your program at?

Explore two illustrative development pathways, then choose a focused engagement tailored to your evidence, timeline and budget. These are examples of how we could work together, not claims of completed client projects.

Your challenge: promising preclinical results, but no clear IND-enabling planPlanning within your budget
01 · DIAGNOSEReview existing dataEfficacy, PK/PD, safety signals, reproducibility, readiness gaps
02 · PRIORITIZEDevelop a research planCritical studies, endpoints, criteria for moving forward, costs and sequencing
03 · SOURCESelect the right CROsTechnical due diligence, bid comparison, scopes and negotiation support
04 · EXECUTEOversee the programMilestones, data review, deviations, reporting and changes to the study plan
05 · TRANSLATEReview and organize study resultsIntegrated data interpretation and nonclinical submission support
Intended impact → A clear, prioritized set of study results and clearer decisions about next steps, with fewer avoidable studies and better alignment between budget, CRO execution and IND requirements. Regulatory, GLP toxicology and CMC specialists remain essential partners.
Your challenge: Phase 1 data are emerging, but Phase 2 decisions remain uncertainPlanning with clinical biomarker data
01 · INTEGRATERead the Phase 1 signalsSafety, exposure, PK/PD, exploratory efficacy and biomarker trends
02 · IDENTIFYFind actionable gapsDose rationale, population, assays, endpoints and key uncertainties
03 · DESIGNPlan the next studiesBiomarker hypotheses, stratification options and evidence priorities
04 · VALIDATERun focused studiesTargeted CRO work, assay suitability and data-quality review
05 · INFORMSupport Phase 2 choicesProtocol discussions, dose/population rationale and clear recommendations for the next study
Intended impact → Better-supported Phase 2 plans, more informative biomarker and patient-selection strategies, and clearer evidence for protocol and development decisions - subject to clinical and statistical review.

Each engagement is tailored to asset modality, available data, regulatory jurisdiction, internal capabilities and budget.

Selected program experience

Research that helped guide clinical programs.

Examples from previous industry work. Outcomes are described at the program level and do not imply sole responsibility for company or clinical decisions.

Clinical biomarker strategy

ctDNA program: connecting Phase 1 evidence with Phase 2 planning

Challenge: Generate clinically relevant biomarker evidence from patient plasma samples to inform subsequent development.

My contribution: Led the biomarker workstream with external CRO partners, coordinated analyses and interpretation, and translated results for development stakeholders.

Program impact: Supported a patient-stratification strategy for randomized Phase 2 planning and contributed to intellectual property and scientific publication work.
Translational pharmacology & safety

FOLFOX neuropathy: connecting preclinical evidence with clinical planning

Challenge: Investigate chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy and potential neuroprotective activity in a clinically relevant setting.

My contribution: Designed and directed an outsourced in vivo research program, coordinated optimization, reviewed data and integrated findings with clinical observations.

Program impact: Generated translational evidence supporting randomized Phase 2 protocol planning and patient-safety considerations, and contributed to patent-related work and scientific dissemination.
